title: Check yourself: Commands, headless runs, auto mode and the practice

questions.stem: A CI job runs `claude -p` to review each diff and must give the same result on every runner. Which flag is the key part?

options.text: `--output-format json`, because it gives a script structured text to parse
options.says: Ruled out because "Use `json` when a script parses the result", which shapes the output and does not remove local configuration.

options.text: `--bare`, because it skips the local setup that discovery finds
options.says: The page says `--bare` is "useful for CI and scripts where you need the same result on every machine."

options.text: `--max-turns`, because it limits how many agentic turns a single run takes
options.says: Ruled out because "`--max-turns` limits the number of agentic turns", which bounds a run and does not make two runners agree.

options.text: `--max-budget-usd`, because it caps the amount that a single run may spend
options.says: Ruled out because "`--max-budget-usd` caps the spend", which is a bound on cost and not on configuration.

questions.stem: A command's workflow deploys code and posts to an external service. How is Claude kept from launching it on its own judgement?

options.text: Add an `argument-hint` line to its frontmatter
options.says: Ruled out because `argument-hint` is "a hint such as `[issue-number]` shown in autocomplete" and controls nobody.

options.text: Save it as a command file and not as a skill folder
options.says: Ruled out because a command file and a skill "both create `/deploy` and work the same way", so the file kind changes nothing.
The page says setting `disable-model-invocation: true` tells it to "prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill", so only a person can start it.
Ruled out because `dontAsk` "runs reads and pre-approved tools and denies anything that would prompt", which decides tool approval and not who may load a command.

questions.stem: A script lists `--allowedTools "Bash"` so that a headless review can run `git diff`. What is wrong with it?

options.text: It pre-approves every shell command, because a bare name matches all
options.says: The trap says "`--allowedTools "Bash"` approves every command. List `Bash(git diff *)` and its like."

options.text: It is rejected at start, because a tool name must carry a pattern
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "List patterns and not whole tools that change things", a recommendation and not a parsing rule, and its own example lists a bare `Read`.

options.text: It is skipped by a bare run, because `--bare` ignores a tool list
options.says: Ruled out because `--bare` skips "auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md", and a flag passed on the command line is not discovered.

options.text: It approves nothing, because only `dontAsk` can pre-approve a tool
options.says: Ruled out because the flag itself "pre-approves specific tools, in quotes and separated by commas", while `dontAsk` merely "runs reads and pre-approved tools".
